thread:
maria: Heads-up — after the kernel selector change to `mha_fused_v2` on canary, streaming chat p99 spiked. Non-streaming completions look fine.

maria: Quick numbers from canary (mb_size=8 for both):
- streaming: p50=80ms p95=220ms p99=480ms
- completions: p50=90ms p95=180ms p99=210ms

maria: I think microbatch sizing + kvcache interaction is the culprit, but want to surface here before I dig deeper.

kevin: thanks for flagging. was the kernel rollout automated? any fallback configured? :eyes:

perf-bot: deploy: kernel `mha_fused_v2` rolled to canary at 2026-03-17T15:04:00Z by release-bot.

kevin: ok. @maria can you paste the profiler flame for a p99 trace? interested in any blocking on kvcache or kernel queue.

maria: attaching condensed trace snippet (simplified):
```
trace_id: 0xabc123
sequence: user->tokenize->kv.load(8 items, 12ms)->kernel(mha_fused_v2, wait 30ms)->kv.store(8 items, 9ms)->stream-send
hotspots: kernel_wait_queue (30-120ms spikes), kvcache.lock_wait (5-20ms)
```

maria: note: the kernel wait queues line up with microbatch boundaries. when mb_size increases, more requests contend for the same fused kernel launch window.

jamal: ran a targeted microbench over the weekend. TL;DR:
- streaming with mb=2: p99 ~ 240ms, throughput ~ 55 req/s per GPU
- streaming with mb=8: p99 ~ 520ms, throughput ~ 80 req/s per GPU (but tail much worse)
- completions (non-streaming) with mb=16: p99 ~ 220ms, throughput ~ 210 req/s per GPU

jamal: so completions can amortize the kernel cost better — tail isn't as sensitive because no streaming flush/emit per token. streaming needs lower mb to keep tail stable.

sophie: i dug into kvcache metrics: when mb>=8 we see per-batch kvcache.update latency jump from median 4ms to 11ms and lock contention increases, likely due to shared cache shards handling larger batched writes. that pairs with the kernel wait time.

sophie: hypothesis: fused kernel increases per-launch throughput but has higher variability for short sequences and interacts poorly with our kvcache shard locking under larger microbatches. fallback kernel `matmul_tiled_v1` is steadier for short-chat workloads.

kevin: makes sense. so for latency SLO (p95/p99) targets we might adopt different microbatch + kernel policies per route: streaming-chat -> mb=2..4 + kernel=fallback; completions -> mb=16 + mha_fused_v2.

maria: agreed. proposed quick config:
```
routes:
  - name: streaming-chat
    mb_size: 2
    kernel_pref: [matmul_tiled_v1, mha_fused_v2]
    kvcache_shard_parallelism: 4
  - name: completions
    mb_size: 16
    kernel_pref: [mha_fused_v2, matmul_tiled_v1]
    kvcache_shard_parallelism: 2
```

jamal: i ran A/B on canary with that config: streaming p99 dropped from 510ms -> 260ms, throughput down ~15% but much tighter tail. completions throughput stayed ~+2x w/ same or better p95.

maria: action items:
- kevin: update kernel rollout to include per-route kernel preferences and rollback to previous selector while we validate. (low-risk toggle)
- jamal: run a sustained 1h soak with synthetic chat workload (seq len dist: 8/50/100) and record p99, kv lock wait histograms.
- sophie: investigate kvcache shard locking — consider async writes or batching rewrite to reduce lock hold time.

kevin: will wire a canary policy change. also add an automatic MB-autotuner experiment: increase mb until p95 degradation > x% or p99 tail crosses SLO.

maria: also note we should update the console perf dashboard to split streaming vs non-streaming microbatch metrics (current aggregate hides this).

sophie: small note: for streaming we might also enable prefix-KV prefetch (disabled currently) to reduce on-path kvcache.load latency — but that risks memory pressure. will simulate.

jamal: log excerpt from the A/B run for anyone debugging:
```
[2026-03-17T15:20:12Z] route=streaming-chat mb=2 kernel=matmul_tiled_v1 req=12345 p99=232ms kv.lock_wait_p99=18ms
[2026-03-17T15:20:12Z] route=streaming-chat mb=8 kernel=mha_fused_v2 req=12355 p99=512ms kv.lock_wait_p99=62ms
[2026-03-17T15:20:12Z] route=completions  mb=16 kernel=mha_fused_v2 req=22345 p99=218ms kv.lock_wait_p99=11ms
```

kevin: perfect. i'll pause further canary rollout of `mha_fused_v2` to default until we have per-route prefs. rolling to a few dedicated canaries for completions-only workloads is fine.

maria: thanks everyone. last thought: we should document recommended defaults for mb by workload type in the perf playbook — helps SEs and customers. i'll draft a PR after the soak results. :memo:

perf-bot: note: issue perf/1846123456 created: "mb tuning: streaming vs completions + kernel prefs"

kevin: closing loop here. if anyone sees regression outside canary ping me. otherwise we proceed with targeted canaries for completions and per-route fallbacks for streaming. :+1:
